---
title: "Expressions"
---

Build column computations with `col()` and the functions in `Phibble\Expr`,
and pass them to table methods. An expression runs on every backend: `DataFrame`
evaluates it, `SqlTable` compiles it to SQL, and `PolarsTable` maps it to
Polars. Each backend follows R's semantics and runs a function in memory when
it has no exact translation. Results can still differ where a database cannot
represent R's value, as [SQL tables](sql.qmd#known-differences) lists.

Table methods also accept PHP closures. A closure can only run in PHP, so a SQL or
Polars table loads its rows to run one.

## Construction {#building-expressions}

`col('price')` reads a column. Methods on any expression build operator
calls, and arguments that are not expressions become literals, as with
`lit(3)`:

| Method | Operator |
| --- | --- |
| `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div`, `mod`, `pow` | `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%%`, `^` |
| `neg` | unary minus |
| `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge` | `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` |
| `and`, `or`, `not` | `&`, <code>&#124;</code>, `!` |
| `isNa()` | `is.na()` |
| `isIn([...])` | `%in%` |
| `between($low, $high)` | `between()` |
| `desc()` | `desc()` |

Functions in the `Phibble\Expr` namespace build the other calls:

- Options are named arguments, as in `mean(col('x'), na_rm: true)` or
  `lag(col('x'), n: 2, default: 0)`.
- `var_()` stands for `var()`, which is a reserved word in PHP.
- A function outside the [list below](#functions) throws when the expression
  is built.

## Expressions in table methods {#using-expressions-with-verbs}

Each method evaluates expressions per group:

- `filter()` keeps rows where the expression is true. NA counts as false.
- `mutate()` adds a column with one value per row. An aggregate such as
  `mean()` gives one value per group, which is repeated for each row of the
  group.
- `summarize()` needs one value per group. Anything else throws a
  `LengthException`.
- `arrange()` sorts by expressions over the whole table, ignoring groups. Wrap
  a key in `desc()` to sort it in descending order.

## Functions

### Scalar functions

Scalar functions return one value per row.

| Function | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `is_na(x)` | True for NA and NaN. |
| `if_else(cond, true, false, missing:)` | `missing` is used where `cond` is NA. |
| `case_when(c1, v1, c2, v2, ..., default:)` | The first true condition wins. NA conditions count as false. |
| `coalesce(x, y, ...)` | The first non-NA value. |
| `x->isIn([...])` | Never NA. NA is in the set only if NA is listed. |
| `between(x, low, high)` | Inclusive. NA if any argument is NA. |
| `na_if(x, y)` | NA where `x == y`. |
| `near(x, y, tol:)` | Equality within a tolerance. |
| `abs`, `sqrt`, `exp`, `log(x, base:)`, `log10`, `floor`, `ceiling` | Math functions. |
| `round(x, digits:)` | Rounds as R 4 does. |
| `as_int`, `as_float`, `as_string`, `as_bool` | Casts with R's `as.*()` rules. |
| `paste0(...)`, `paste(..., sep:)` | NA becomes the text `NA`, as in R. |

### Text functions (stringr)

As in stringr, a pattern given as text is a regular expression. phibble uses
PCRE and matches by Unicode character; stringr uses ICU, and the two agree on
common patterns. `fixed('...')` matches the text literally, and
`regex('...', ignore_case: true)` sets options.

| Function | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `str_detect`, `str_starts`, `str_ends` (with `negate:`) | `str_starts` and `str_ends` anchor the pattern. |
| `str_count(x, pattern)` | Non-overlapping matches. |
| `str_extract(x, pattern)` | The first match, or NA. |
| `str_extract_all(x, pattern)`, `str_split(x, pattern)` | A list-column. NA gives a list holding NA. |
| `str_split_i(x, pattern, i)` | The i-th piece; negative `i` counts from the end; NA when out of range. |
| `str_replace`, `str_replace_all` | `\1` in the replacement refers to a group. An NA replacement gives NA where the pattern matches. |
| `str_pad(x, width, side:, pad:)` | `side` is `left` (default), `right`, or `both`. |
| `str_trunc(x, width, side:, ellipsis:)` | `side` is `right` (default), `left`, or `center`. |
| `str_to_upper`, `str_to_lower`, `str_to_title`, `str_squish` | Title case capitalizes after a hyphen but not after an apostrophe, as ICU does. |
| `str_length`, `str_trim(x, side:)`, `str_sub(x, start, end)` | `str_sub` is 1-based and inclusive; negative positions count from the end. |
| `str_lower`, `str_upper` | Aliases of `str_to_lower` and `str_to_upper`. |

### Dates and times (lubridate)

Date functions accept dates and datetimes, and a date stays a date: results
such as `floor_date(d, 'month')` or `d + days(1)` are dates when `d` is.

| Function | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `ymd`, `dmy`, `mdy`, `ymd_hms`, `dmy_hms`, `mdy_hms` (with `tz:`) | Parse text. Separators are optional; invalid input gives NA. |
| `parse_date_time(x, orders, tz:)` | Orders made of `Y`, `y`, `m`, `d`, `H`, `M`, and `S`, such as `'Ymd HMS'`; the first that fits wins. |
| `year`, `month`, `day`, `yday`, `quarter`, `hour`, `minute`, `second` | Parts as numbers. On a time, `hour()`, `minute()`, and `second()` give its clock time, and the date parts throw. |
| `wday(x, week_start:)` | 1 is Sunday by default, as in lubridate; `week_start: 1` makes Monday 1. |
| `floor_date`, `ceiling_date`, `round_date` (`x, unit, week_start:`) | Units from `second` to `year`, with multiples such as `'15 minutes'`. `ceiling_date` moves a date that is already on a boundary to the next one, as lubridate does for dates. |
| `seconds`, `minutes`, `hours`, `days`, `weeks`, `months`, `years` | Periods, used as `col('d')->add(months(1))`. Month and year arithmetic that lands on a date that does not exist gives NA. |
| `difftime(x, y, units:)` | A number in `secs`, `mins`, `hours`, `days` (default), or `weeks`. `date - date` gives days and `datetime - datetime` seconds. |
| `with_tz(x, tz)`, `force_tz(x, tz)` | The same instant in another zone; the same clock time in another zone (NA for a time the zone skips). |
| `today(tz:)`, `now(tz:)` | Read `Phibble\Expr\Clock`, which tests can freeze. |

### Aggregates

An aggregate returns one value per group. Each takes `na_rm:`, which is false
by default, so an aggregate over a group containing NA returns NA unless
`na_rm: true`.

| Function | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `n()` | Rows in the group. |
| `sum`, `mean`, `median`, `min`, `max` | `sum` of no values is 0 and `mean` is NaN. |
| `sd`, `var_` | Sample statistics, with `n - 1`. |
| `quantile(x, p)`, `iqr(x)` | R's default type 7. These throw on NA unless `na_rm: true`, as R does. |
| `n_distinct(x, ...)` | Counts NA as a value unless `na_rm: true`. Takes several columns. |
| `first`, `last`, `nth(x, n)` | Take `default:` and `order_by:`. Negative `n` counts from the end. |
| `any`, `all` | Three-valued, as in R. |

### Window functions

A window function returns one value per row, computed over the rows of the
group in row order.

| Function | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `lag(x, n:, default:, order_by:)`, `lead(...)` | Shift values within the group. |
| `row_number(x)` | Ranks with ties broken by position. Without `x`, the row's position. |
| `min_rank`, `dense_rank`, `percent_rank`, `cume_dist` | NA values stay NA and are not counted. Pass `desc(x)` to rank in descending order. |
| `ntile(x, n:)` | Splits rows into `n` groups of nearly equal size, larger groups first. |
| `cumsum`, `cumprod`, `cummean`, `cummin`, `cummax` | Every value after the first NA is NA. |
| `cumall`, `cumany` | Follow dplyr's NA rules. |
| `consecutive_id(...)` | Increments when any argument changes. |

## NA and arithmetic

Expressions follow R's rules for missing values and arithmetic:

- Arithmetic and comparisons with NA give NA.
- `&` and `|` use three-valued logic. `FALSE & NA` is false and `TRUE | NA` is
  true.
- `/` and `^` always return floats. Division by zero gives `Inf`, `-Inf`, or
  `NaN`.
- `%%` takes the sign of the divisor, so `-7 %% 3` is 2.
- `round()` takes, of the two candidates, the one closer to the stored value,
  and an exact tie goes to the even digit. `round(2.5)` is 2, and
  `round(2.675, digits: 2)` is 2.67 because 2.675 is stored as slightly less
  than 2.675.
- Text compares and sorts in byte order.

{{< include examples/_expr-na.md >}}

## Expression trees

This section is for code that inspects, stores, or translates expressions.
An expression is a tree of four kinds of node:

- `Col` reads a column.
- `Lit` holds a literal value: a number, text, a date, or a list of values for
  `isIn()`.
- `Call` applies a registered function to arguments. `call('name', ...)`
  builds one by name.
- `Desc` marks a sort key or ranking as descending.

`columns()` lists the columns an expression reads, and `toArray()` returns the
tree as plain arrays:

{{< include examples/_expr-build.md >}}

`Phibble\Expr\Functions::REGISTRY` lists every function a `Call` may name,
with its arguments and options.

### Serialization

`toArray()` returns a JSON-friendly array, and `Expr::fromArray()` rebuilds the
expression. Each node has a `type` key: `col`, `lit`, `call`, or `desc`. A call
lists its positional arguments under `args` and its options under `named`. A
date literal carries `dtype` (`date`, `datetime`, or `time`).

{{< include examples/_expr-roundtrip.md >}}

### Reference tests

`tests/r/expr.R` evaluates the test expressions in dplyr and stores the
results in `tests/fixtures/expr/expected.json`. The test suite checks
`DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, and `PolarsTable` against them.
